descriptionHtml:
Approach · OAT-06 Measuring How the Pilot Is Working (Usage Analytics) · S17 Existing api specs: every AI call kind logs the vendor's time beside the total; on a stubbed fallback the log and audit rows name the answering model

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U13 Every AI call (pre-round summary, note generation, billing, Ask AI, photo capture, handoff) logs its total time and, separately, the time the AI provider itself took, and which model answered (UAT 3.5; UAT 3.9; TFA-94514 AC 7)

Test design technique: Performance (performance) — Measure the time and check it is within the required seconds.

Given Local backend, diagnostics cleared before each kind; a logged invocation with bedrock.invoke stubbed for the fallback

When Call parsePreRoundNotes, generateNote, suggestBilling, askChart, scanCensusSheet, generateHandoff; run a stubbed Haiku -> Mistral fallback and a normal Haiku call

Then aiCallLog providerMs is a number and durationMs >= providerMs for the six kinds; the ai_disclosure audit row's provider_ms is checked for notes.generateNote only. On the stubbed fallback the log row has model Mistral, fellBackFrom Haiku, ok true, and the audit row model Mistral, fell_back_from Haiku; the normal path has model Haiku and no fellBackFrom. …

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Playwright api assertions. Without vendor credentials the six kinds fail and are timed anyway, so live timing is S04 / S07 / S10 / S18 / S19. Other call types (transcription, voice fix, extraction) are Q13

Where it ran: local lane A (existing Playwright tests); test method API · API (Convex functions); lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (automated)

S17 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-06.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: local — main e02167f, local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane A.

Test method: API · API (Convex functions); secondary: PERF · Performance timing — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: matrix (lane A).

UAT item: OAT-06 Measuring How the Pilot Is Working (Usage Analytics) · Section: B · Operational Acceptance Tests · Scenario: OAT-06/S17

Existing api specs: every AI call kind logs the vendor's time beside the total; on a stubbed fallback the log and audit rows name the answering model

Tickets: TFA-94514 Analytics tracking (ready for qa)

Result: passed in matrix/OAT-06.results.json (lane A: the existing Playwright specs below, run on the local stack; agent-matrix.sh).

Existing specs:

  • api/ai-call-timing.spec.ts [api] — an AI call's log row and audit row carry the total and the vendor's time — expected
  • api/ai-call-timing.spec.ts [api] — every kind of AI call item 7 names logs the vendor's time — expected
  • api/provider-fallback.spec.ts [api] — PF-04-01 log shows the answering model — expected
  • api/provider-fallback.spec.ts [api] — PF-04-01 log shows the answering model (twin): no fallback, Haiku and no fellBackFrom — expected
  • api/provider-fallback.spec.ts [api] — PF-04-02 audit row shows it too — expected
  • api/provider-fallback.spec.ts [api] — PF-04-02 audit row shows it too (twin): the normal path has no fell_back_from — expected

Dev run: skipped: local-only — local-only — Lane A runs Tim's api specs ai-call-timing.spec.ts and provider-fallback.spec.ts, which call the six AI actions directly and stub bedrock.invoke in a logged invocation on the local backend, then read the audit rows with the admin key; on dev the runner calls no action, stubs nothing and has no ad…. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
